items.before:
A BASE II processing center acting in support of one or more issuers. The
processing center processes completed account holder transactions (local
and interchange) for account holder account posting and billing. For
completed interchange transactions, the center is also responsible for
receiving and processing incoming transactions for the account holders of
the issuer or issuers.
items.after:
A BASE II processing center acting in support of one or more issuers.
The processing center processes completed cardholder transactions (local
and interchange) for cardholder account posting and billing. For completed
interchange transactions, the center is also responsible for receiving and
processing incoming transactions for the cardholders of the issuer or issuers.
items.reason: El cambio modifica el término 'account holder' por 'cardholder' y 'account posting' por 'cardholder account posting', lo que altera el significado de negocio en el contexto de los procesos de facturación y procesamiento.

items.before:
A numeric value used to define issuing processing. Multiple Issuing BINs can
be linked to the same Issuing Identifier in Visa's systems.
items.after:
A numeric value used to define issuing processing. It is not governed by ISO
and does not have to start with a four (4). Multiple issuing BINs can be linked
to the same issuing identifier within Visa systems, which can allow mirroring
of processing or routing configurations.
items.reason: El texto nuevo especifica que el Issuing Identifier no está gobernado por ISO y no debe comenzar con un 4, lo que modifica su definición comercial.

items.before: X X X X X card-not-present transactions only) 1For Visa, purchase with cashback is allowed for domestic transactions only; it is not supported for interna­ tional transactions. Acquirers in the U.S. region that do not participate in real-time clearing (RTC) must follow 0100 Visa AFD transactions with an 0120 acquirer confirmation advice that contains the actual transaction amount. If the issuer supports 0120 confirmation advices, VisaNet forwards the message to the issuer. If the issuer does not support these advices, VisaNet processes the transaction in STIP and responds to the acquirer with an 0130 message. Issuers must be able to support AFD status check and confirmation advices. In these messages, field 25 must contain valid values other than 06, which should only be received in real-time clearing fuel transactions. Acquirers must not submit Mastercard POS 02xx full financial messages. For AFD completions destined for Mastercard, acquirers must use 0120 messages. Merchants and acquirers must send the final amount to VisaNet within 2 hours of the preauthorization. For Mastercard AFD transactions in Visa Canada and in the U.S. region, the final amount must be sent within 1 hour of the preauthorization. Acquirers must not submit Mastercard POS 02xx full financial messages. For AFD completions destined for Mastercard, acquirers must use 0120 messages. If an issuer sends an 0230 preauthorization completion advice response with a decline response code, V.I.P. checks the transaction history. If the original preauthorization request was declined or not received by the issuer, V.I.P. processes the decline from the issuer. If V.I.P. processes an 0220 preauthorization completion in STIP, and the transaction history indicates that the corresponding preauthorization request was declined, V.I.P. declines the 0220 preauthorization completion. If the merchant does not submit a completion message within 2 hours of sending the preauthorization request message, V.I.P. generates a preauthorization reversal on behalf of the acquirer and delivers it to the issuer. V.I.P. also generates a 0420 reversal advice for the acquirer and places it in its advice queue. Merchants should support partial authorizations, which allow the issuer to approve an amount below the original estimated authorization amount.
